original_tex:
GW170817~\cite{Abbott2017GW170817} placed an extraordinarily tight
bound on $\cGW$: comparing the gravitational-wave arrival time at
LIGO/Virgo against the gamma-ray-burst signal at Fermi/INTEGRAL,
the multi-messenger collaboration constrained
$-3 \times 10^{-15} \leq \dccap \leq +7 \times 10^{-16}$.
Conservatively two-sided, $|\dccap| \leq \tau$ with
$\tau = 3 \times 10^{-15}$.
exact_proposal_tex:
GW170817~\cite{Abbott2017GW170817} yielded a tight propagation
constraint under the collaboration's conservative distance and
emission-time assumptions. Comparing the gravitational-wave arrival
time at LIGO/Virgo with the gamma-ray signal at Fermi/INTEGRAL gives
$-3 \times 10^{-15} \leq \dccap \leq +7 \times 10^{-16}$
under those assumptions. We use its conservative symmetric envelope,
$|\dccap| \leq \tau$ with $\tau = 3 \times 10^{-15}$.
This cap inherits the assumed source-emission window; alternative
emission histories can weaken the inferred propagation constraint.
source_assumptions: Section 4 uses observed offset, source distance and expected emission-time difference, rather than observed offset alone.
Section 4.1 chooses 26 Mpc, the lower end of the 90% GW luminosity-distance credible interval, because smaller distances give weaker constraints.
Upper endpoint assumes simultaneous GW peak and first-photon emission; lower endpoint assumes the SGRB was emitted 10 seconds after the GW signal.
Eq. (1) is exactly the cited asymmetric range. The symmetric tau=3e-15 envelope is a conservative manuscript choice containing that range.
Section 4.1 explicitly discusses longer delays and pre-merger photons; its alternative window broadens the allowed velocity interval on both sides.
The section closes by identifying emission times as model dependent and future joint observations as a route to separating emission and propagation effects.
